instruction: In the opened movies spreadsheet, create a new sheet called 'movies_90s' containing only movies released between 1990 and 1999. Keep the same column headers and sort the results by ratings from highest to lowest.

command: import pyautogui; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); import time; time.sleep(1)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent created an 'unseen_movies' sheet but copied ALL seen_movies data instead of finding unseen IMDB Top 30 movies. Never visited IMDB website. Attempted to sort data in the new sheet.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can create new sheets in LibreOffice Calc, copy data between sheets, use sort dialog, navigate between sheet tabs, right-click context menus
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because it never visited IMDB to get the Top 30 list. Instead, it copied all existing seen_movies to unseen_movies sheet. The cross-application comparison (Chrome + Calc) was too complex.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single-app LibreOffice Calc task: filter movies by decade. No external website needed. Within model's demonstrated capability of sheet creation and data manipulation.
metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new sheet with 1990s movies sorted by rating. Evaluator checks: sheet exists with correct name, headers match, row count is 30, all rows have release year in [1990,1999], and data is sorted by ratings descending. [Fixed: normalized getter row dict keys to lowercase for case-insensitive sort_key/year_key lookup; added year range verification check]

scoring_breakdown.headers_match: 0.25 - Headers match original (title, release year, ratings, description)
scoring_breakdown.year_range: 0.125 - All rows have release year between 1990 and 1999
scoring_breakdown.sort_order: 0.25 - Sorted by ratings from highest to lowest

fix_history: Fix 1: Normalized getter row dict keys to lowercase to fix case-sensitive sort_key/year_key lookup bug
Fix 2: Added year range verification (1990-1999) to metric with 0.125 weight
Fix 3: Rebalanced scoring: row_count reduced from 0.25 to 0.125, year_range added at 0.125

llm_judge_reasons: All 4 instruction requirements are verified: (1) sheet name 'movies_90s' checked case-insensitively (0.25), (2) year range [1990,1999] verified for all rows (0.125), (3) headers match checked case-insensitively (0.25), (4) descending sort by ratings verified (0.25).
Getter correctly normalizes row dict keys to lowercase, ensuring consistent lookup for year_key='release year' and sort_key='ratings' regardless of original header capitalization.
Expected parameter handling is correct: metric receives the rules dict directly (type='rule') and accesses fields like expected.get('expected_sheet_name') without nesting errors.
Postconfig properly activates the window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation, ensuring fresh file state is read.
Minor note: expected_row_count=30 is unverifiable without the source data, but the logic itself is sound and the row count check provides reasonable partial credit with a tolerance of ±2.
